messages:
Anya: quick sync — I'm drafting a short playbook for handing a new quant profile from q-team -> Optimize -> runtime. want to capture naming, manifest, semantic versioning, and consumer compatibility checks. thoughts?
Matt: +1, this has been fuzzy. we should force a single canonical manifest field for compatibility, e.g. `compat: [runtime_versions]` so runtime can opt-in/skip.
Carmen: agree. also call out golden evals and accuracy delta thresholds in the manifest (`quality_gate`) so autoscaler/rollout hooks can make decisions.
Lee: can we keep names readable for ops? something like `model-x_v1.3_awq-int8.qprof` felt ok in bakeoffs but ergonomics matter.
Anya: that's the debate — machine-friendly vs human-friendly. proposal: filename = `model-semantics.qprof` and manifest contains `pkg_name`, `pkg_version` (semver), `format` (awq/gptq/int8/fp8), `variant` (if any).
Sam: quick example manifest (draft):
```
name: redwood/llama-3-13b
pkg_version: 1.2.0
format: awq
precision: int8
compat: ["runtime>=2.4.0", "redispatch>=1.1"]
quality_gate:
  eval_suite: "regressions/core-v2"
  max_p0_drop: 0.015
release_notes: "AWQ int8 profile from bakeoff, see qprof-id: qprof-20240715-11"
```
Anya: Open question: should `pkg_version` follow semver strictly and bump minor on non-breaking perf improvements? Carmen?
Carmen: yes semver is fine. We treat format/precision changes as potentially breaking — bump major. Small tuning/threshold shifts = patch or minor depending on consumer impact. document examples.
Lee: runtime-side, we want `format` + `quant_hash` to map to specific kernel choices. maybe include `runtime_hint` with `scheduler` preferences.
Matt: also add a `rollout_policy` block for Optimize to orchestrate canary sizes + fallback profiles. example: `{canary: 5%, metric: "p0_latency", rollback_if: ">=0.1"}`
OptimizeBot: heads-up: Optimize will read fields `quality_gate` and `rollout_policy` for automated experiments if present. Missing fields will use defaults.
Sam: +question — where do we publish artifacts? S3 path recommended + checksum. add `artifact_url` and `sha256`.
Anya: yes add both. also include `consumer_hints` list — e.g., `requires_kv_cache: true`, `prefers_batching: low_latency` so consumer teams can choose profile automatically.
Carmen: for naming/versioning policy doc section: 1) pkg_name uses org/model-name; 2) pkg_version semver; 3) format tag in manifest (not filename); 4) filename ends with `.qprof` and can contain short label but must not be the source of truth.
Lee: runtime will validate `sha256` before accepting. add a small `compat_test` url or a CI badge link to indicate the profile passed canonical smoke tests.
Matt: ops ask — how to handle forked profiles for customer-specific tuning? Maybe `channel: public|private|enterprise` and an `owner` field.
Anya: good call. add `visibility` and `owners`.
Sam: i'm going to prototype a small `qprof-validator` that checks manifest semantics + runs the compatibility matrix. PR later today.
Anya: sweet. next steps: Sam drafts validator + example manifests; Carmen writes a short section on quality gates and threshold rationale; Matt + Lee sketch rollout_policy defaults; I'll collate into a single short playbook and publish to docs.
Matt: tagging folks @here — if you have specific constraints for runtime mapping or Optimize integrations, drop them here by EOD.
OptimizeBot: action created: OPT-1243 "qprofile manifest schema + validator" assigned to Sam. ETA 2 days.
Carmen: small nit — include a recommended `eval_inputs` pointer (e.g. dataset name + seed) so we can repro quality deltas during rollouts.
Anya: added to doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks, will send initial PR in ~3hrs.
